title: Silent degradation detection and dashboard healing playbook
creator: Asha Menon
description: This ticket consolidates follow-ups from a recent capacity/regression incident where the Console surface showed healthy aggregates while a subset of tenants experienced silent degradation (increased tail latency and retry amplification). We observed multiple dashboard and tracing gaps that prevented early detection and escalations. The goal is to add detection signals, fix visualizations, and codify a playbook so future silent-degradation modes are detected and remedied before user-facing errors escalate.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-16 at ~10:12 UTC a spike in tail latency impacted a subset of tenants using Dedicated pools. The platform-level SLOs did not breach; however, tenant-level 99.9th latency increased 3x for roughly 8% of active tenants over a 45-minute window. Existing Console dashboards and alerting aggregated across tenants and sampling suppressed the signal, so on-call did not receive an actionable page until errors appeared in customer dashboards. Root cause surfaced as a combination of a regressed kernel-path that increased KV cache eviction pressure under large-sequence batched workloads plus a silent retry loop in a downstream dataplane consumer.
root_cause_analysis:
1) Missing per-tenant high-percentile latency metrics: dashboards were built on 95th percentiles and aggregates which masked tail anomalies.
2) Sampling/quota on tracing: distributed traces were sampled at 1% for high-throughput endpoints; eviction path traces were not captured during the incident window.
3) No synthetic/heartbeat checks for per-tenant steady-state latency: we lacked automated heatcheck probes that emulate customer request distributions.
4) Alerts used static thresholds tuned to global load, causing low signal-to-noise for tenant-local regressions.
5) Runbook did not define escalation for latency-only degradations without error-rate changes.
decisions: Add per-tenant 95/99/99.9 latency percentiles (and token-count normalized variants) to Console metrics pipeline.
Increase trace sampling for critical KV-eviction and batch paths to 10% by default, with dynamic on-demand capture when heatchecks detect anomalies.
Introduce adaptive alerting: baseline per-tenant dynamic thresholds using rolling-window percentiles (p99 vs historical p95) rather than fixed buckets.
Create a minimal synthetic heatcheck job per tenant class (small/medium/large) that runs at 1m cadence and writes results to a dedicated insights index.
Refactor affected dashboard panels to surface tenant-level tails and a coarse map of 'affected tenant set' to support fast Triage.
Bundle changes into console-2026.03 release with a monitoring migration window and one-week staggered rollout.
Add a new runbook section 'Silent Degradation' outlining detection, mitigation, and rollback steps.

acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant p95/p99/p99.9 metrics are emitted and visible in Console for live and historical windows.
Heatcheck jobs run for each tenant class and surface automated anomalies in the new dashboard index.
Tracing sampling for critical spans is increased and on-demand snapshotting works without exceeding cardinality caps.
Adaptive alerts trigger pages for tenant-local tail regressions during the rollout window and escalate correctly.
Runbook published and linked from the Console dashboard with at least two on-call engineers trained on playbook steps.
